subject: Observability stack consolidation — timelines, cost tradeoffs, and 30-day retention decision
messages:
From: Ben Howard <ben.howard@acmecorp.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Observability renewal cycle — options for cost reduction

Vivek / team,

Our observability contracts are up for renewal in Q4 and finance asked me to explore consolidation options across Datadog, Grafana Cloud and Sentry. Current ask: reduce recurring spend by ~30% without losing SLO-level telemetry for customer-facing services.

What I can share now:
- Monthly spend (all products): ~$62k
- Datadog APM + logs ~ $38k/mo
- Grafana Cloud (metrics + traces) ~$14k/mo
- Sentry (errors) ~$10k/mo

We'd like to understand:
1) Tradeoffs if we move log retention from 90d -> 30d (ingest vs storage).
2) Potential discounts for committing 12 months vs month-to-month.
3) Any operational work to move dashboards / alerts.

Happy to set a short call. Sending to Lauren to help with numbers.

Thanks,
Ben
Sr. Engineering Manager, Acme Retail

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ben Howard <ben.howard@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability renewal cycle — options for cost reduction

Ben — thanks for the summary. Good framing.

We can run a short side-by-side on:
- Cost with 30d vs 90d retention (tokens: logs, metrics, traces).
- What functionality would be impacted by lower retention (alerts/ML anomaly detection, ad-hoc debugging).
- Contract levers: committed usage, tiering, and cross-product bundling (Datadog + Grafana discounts are often negotiable).

Lauren — can you produce an initial delta model (3 scenarios: keep current, reduce retention to 30d, consolidate logs into one provider with 30d) and attach vendor quotes? Naomi / Karthik — please flag any procurement/finance constraints (SLA needs, legal clause blockers).

I'll also reach out to Emma at Datadog and Grafana sales; want to give them a week to respond before we push a recommendation to Acme.

— Vivek
VP, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Howard <ben.howard@acmecorp.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-20T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability renewal cycle — options for cost reduction

Attaching a quick model and vendor stubs. Summary (high level):

Scenario A — Status quo (90d retention, multi-vendor): $62k/mo
Scenario B — 30d retention across all (no consolidation): $48k/mo (approx 22% savings)
Scenario C — Consolidate logs into single provider + 30d retention: $37k/mo (40% savings) but migration effort ~3-4 wks and potential short-term alert noise.

Key notes:
- Datadog provided a preliminary 18% discount for a 12-month commit (see Datadog-quote-2027-07.pdf).
- Grafana offered product credits for cross-product adoption; their baseline for logs is cheaper but lacks some APM features.
- Sentry can offer a usage-based cap; see Sentry-usage-export.csv for current error volumes.

Attachments: Datadog-quote-2027-07.pdf (PDF, 120KB), Grafana-Proposal-2027-07.docx (DOCX, 90KB), Sentry-usage-export.csv (CSV, 45KB)

Next steps I propose:
- Internal decision on retention (30d vs 90d) by EOW Jul 22
- Ask vendors for formal 12-month committed quotes by Jul 26
- If we choose consolidation, schedule migration window Sept 6–17 (non-prod first)

-lb
Lauren Bishop
Product Finance

From: Emma Barnes <emma@datadog.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Howard <ben.howard@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2027-07-21T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability renewal cycle — options for cost reduction

Hi all —

Thanks for the details and the model. A couple quick clarifications from Datadog's side:
- The 18% preliminary discount Lauren referenced assumes no significant increase in peak ingest. If Acme consolidates logs into Datadog we can go to 28% with a 12-month commit + add-on commitment (we'll need an approximate committed ingest number).
- For 30d retention, some enterprise features (long-running log-based analytics and certain audit searches) are impacted; we can scope workarounds (export hooks to cold storage).

We can produce a formal committed-usage amendment and a migration checklist; happy to join a call next week.

Emma Barnes
Enterprise Sales — Datadog
emma@datadog.com | +1 415-555-0199

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Howard <ben.howard@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2027-07-22T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability renewal cycle — options for cost reduction

Team — quick decision note from procurement/finance:

1) Move forward with 30-day retention as default for logs (exceptions for legal/audit services documented).
2) Ask Datadog to produce a committed 12-month quote at the 28% level and provide committed ingest numbers by Jul 26.
3) Parallel run: request Grafana to price metric+trace only bundle and Sentry to cap error spend.

Action owners: Lauren (vendor quotes & cost model) — due Jul 26; Vivek (vendor coordination & decision memo to Acme) — due Jul 28; Naomi (contract/legal redlines) — due Aug 2.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Procurement
Redwood Inference
